title: Inflammatory or malignant? The establishment of a molecular classifier to differentiate early Mycosis fungoides from benign inflammatory dermatoses.
summary:
Mycosis fungoides (MF) is the most common type of a rare skin lymphoma. It is often hard to tell apart from harmless inflammatory skin diseases — even with today’s best diagnostic tools.

Since the treatment approaches are very different — early MF often requires a wait-and-see approach, while inflammatory skin diseases may need strong treatment early on — getting the diagnosis right as soon as possible is very important.

To enable more personalized treatment in the future, we need a deeper understanding of the molecular causes of MF. In this study, we will analyze blood and tissue samples from MF patients in the Freiburg Dermatology Registry using modern techniques like RNA sequencing, PCR, and ELISA. The goal is to develop a test that can reliably distinguish MF from other skin conditions.
